title: A river port on the east coast
body: Read the passage and answer the question. A major port on the east coast of India stands on the Hugli river, about 128 km inland from the Bay of Bengal. Like Mumbai, it was developed by the British, and it gained an early advantage because the city was the capital of British India. Over time, the port lost much of its significance as exports were diverted to Vishakhapatnam, Paradwip and a satellite port built 105 km downstream. The river that links the port to the sea keeps depositing silt, which has to be removed for ships to reach it. Its hinterland covers Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Sikkim and the north-eastern states, and it also serves the land-locked neighbouring countries Nepal and Bhutan.
